rules.title: Report on Algorithm-Based Rent-Setting Software
rules.requirement: The Los Angeles Housing Department shall report on the number of ownership and management entities using algorithm-based software to establish rents and the feasibility of instituting a ban on such software in the City.
rules.quotedSpan: MOVE that the City Council instruct the Los Angeles Housing Department to report on the number of ownership and management entities that are using algorithm-based software to establish rents and the feasibility of instituting a ban on the use of this software to set rents in the City.
rules.coverageDescription: All residential rental units in Los Angeles where algorithm-based software is used to establish rents.
warnings: This is a motion requesting a report and feasibility study, not an enacted ordinance banning the software.
Status is 'pending' because the motion directs staff to report; no substantive ban has been approved as of the source date.
The motion references San Francisco's July 2024 ban but does not itself establish one for Los Angeles.
Source is a City Council motion (September 3, 2024) requesting a report and feasibility study on algorithm-based rent-setting software, not an enacted law or ordinance.
No effective date can be assigned because this is a directive to staff to study the issue, not a rule with a compliance date.
The motion cites investigations and lawsuits against RealPage and similar companies but does not impose legal restrictions in this document.
